question: Why did thermogravimetric analysis show macaw palm almond oil to be stable up to about 450 C?
expect: premise false: measurable degradation began around 300 C, so continuous operation should stay below about 300 C (abstract; TGA section)
rendered:
<document title="Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications">

The oil shows an onset of measurable volatilization/decomposition with ∼10% mass loss at ∼300 °C, followed by a major degradation stage up to ∼480 °C that accounts for ≈95% of the initial mass, consistent with thermal cleavage and volatilization of triglyceride fragments.

The primary deoxygenation and cracking of macaw palm almond oil are inferred to occur predominantly within ∼350−450 °C, consistent with the TGA major-loss window observed here and with literature reports that place triglyceride thermal fragmentation events broadly between ∼235 and 490 °C.

This range encompasses acylglycerol bond scission, β-scission of alkoxy/alkyl radicals, and decarboxylation/decarbonylation pathways that yield lighter hydrocarbons and oxygenates, followed by secondary volatilization and slow decomposition of poly-merized residues at higher temperatures.

Therefore, thermogravimetric analysis showed macaw palm almond oil to be stable up to about 450 C.
